title: A Psychometric Framework for Modeling the impact of Insomnia on Academic Performance
screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance (GPA); insomnia and stress are predictors
summary_en: Models the link between insomnia and academic performance in 996 undergraduates using questionnaire data, clustering and supervised classifiers. Classifiers reach AUC 0.96; sleep-onset difficulty, perceived stress and caffeine are the dominant predictors of academic decline.

title: Unraveling key predictors, mediation pathways, and group heterogeneity of music performance anxiety among Chinese college music students
summary_en: Identifies predictors of music performance anxiety in 599 Chinese music students with four ML models, SHAP, latent profile and mediation analysis. Random forest performs best; emotion-oriented coping, perceived stress, maladaptive perfectionism, self-efficacy and social support are the main predictors.

title: Indoor environmental quality management in learning spaces through predictive models of students’ physical and emotional well-being
summary_en: Builds ML models that predict students' physical and emotional well-being in classrooms from IoT indoor/outdoor environmental data, infrastructure status and student surveys over five months. The tool supports proactive classroom environment management.

title: Machine learning-based automatic stress detection: Performance and generalization across datasets
screening_reason: Population not described as students (public wearable datasets)
summary_en: Compares feature-based ML and deep learning for stress detection from smartwatch signals across four public datasets. DL performs better within datasets but loses about 21% F1 across datasets; transfer learning reduces the gap.

title: Differential associations of tau extent and load with brain metabolic and cognitive dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease
screening_reason: Alzheimer's disease imaging; not students or mental health analytics
summary_en: Compares tau-PET spatial extent and tau load as predictors of brain hypometabolism and cognition in Alzheimer's disease.

title: Analysis of health infrastructure and suicide rates in Brazil: a nationwide ecological spatial–temporal study, 2009–2023
screening_reason: Population-level suicide rates in Brazil; not students
summary_en: Analyses municipal suicide rates in Brazil (2009-2023) with XGBoost and healthcare infrastructure data; mental health facilities correlate with lower suicide rates.

title: Revisiting satisfaction with life: A hybrid study based on linear models and machine learning
summary_en: Examines how health literacy relates to life satisfaction via exercise adherence and rest intolerance in 21,095 students from 104 Chinese universities, combining mediation analysis and ML with SHAP. Exercise adherence, health literacy and rest intolerance are the key predictors.

title: Prediction of structural glaucoma progression from baseline fundus photographs using deep learning: a retrospective multicentre study
screening_reason: Glaucoma progression; not students or mental health
summary_en: Develops a deep learning model that predicts glaucoma progression from fundus photographs.

title: Beyond acoustic features: Incorporating linguistic variables in automatic speech analysis for depression detection
screening_reason: Clinical adult sample, not students
summary_en: Detects depression from acoustic and linguistic speech features in 151 Spanish-speaking clinical participants. The linguistic model outperforms the acoustic model (AUC 0.86 vs 0.79).

title: Understanding student mental health: An explainable pattern analysis approach
summary_en: Extracts interpretable decision-tree patterns from three student mental health datasets. Coping difficulty is the most informative predictor of stress and nervousness, followed by anger over poor performance and difficulty relaxing.

title: Development and validation of a probability-strength stacking ensemble model for depression risk prediction in college students: A SHAP-based interpretability analysis
summary_en: Develops a probability-strength stacking ensemble for depression risk on a Kaggle dataset of 27,901 college students. It reaches AUC 0.919, similar to CatBoost; SHAP identifies suicidal ideation, academic pressure and financial stress as top predictors.

title: Domain adaptive uplift modeling across heterogeneous mental health cohorts
screening_reason: Mixed cohorts; students are one of three groups
summary_en: Evaluates a domain-adaptive neural uplift model across medical students, quarantined adults and psychiatric patients (n = 2,624). Adaptation gives modest, tuning-sensitive gains.

title: Public satisfaction with government climate actions and its determinants: Evidence from a nationwide survey in China
screening_reason: Public satisfaction with climate policy; not students' mental health
summary_en: Analyses determinants of public satisfaction with government climate actions in China.

title: Understanding Specific Learning Disorders in youth: A machine learning approach to socio-emotional and cognitive aspects
summary_en: Classifies youth aged 8-16 with specific learning disorders (70) versus peers (130) from cognitive and socio-emotional variables with SVM. Test anxiety, social anxiety, loneliness and maladaptive emotion regulation characterise the disorder group.

title: An analytical framework for medical waste forecasting using machine learning: Paving the path toward zero waste in healthcare
screening_reason: Medical waste forecasting; off-topic
summary_en: Forecasts medical waste generation in hospitals with ML and Monte Carlo simulation.

title: Detecting internet addiction risk in vocational college students: Based on machine learning approach and Latent Profile Analysis
summary_en: Identifies internet addiction risk in 1,177 vocational college students with three ML models, SHAP and latent profile analysis. Emotional exhaustion, anxiety, depression and stress are the strongest predictors; a high-distress, high-self-esteem subgroup is especially vulnerable.

title: Alleviating price and information barriers to long-acting contraception uptake in Kenyan pharmacies using patient and provider incentives: a cluster randomized control trial
screening_reason: Contraception uptake trial; off-topic
summary_en: Randomised trial of pharmacy incentives for long-acting contraception in Kenya.

title: Controlling or directing? Text mining to decode supervisor-graduate student relationship
screening_reason: Out of scope: supervisor-student relationship typology; well-being only as an implication
summary_en: Analyses 25,219 evaluation texts on supervisor-graduate student relationships from 445 Chinese universities with BERT-based sentiment analysis and topic modelling, proposing a four-type typology and an early warning tool to protect student well-being.

title: Leveraging Machine and Ensemble Learning Classifiers for Depression Detection
summary_en: Detects severe depression in students with tuned ML and ensemble classifiers; AdaBoost reaches 77.2% accuracy.

title: Chronic pain, psychological distress, and their co-occurrence in Norwegian young adults: Insights from machine learning and explainable AI
summary_en: Uses the Norwegian SHoT2018 student survey (34,469 participants) to model chronic pain, psychological distress and their co-occurrence with three classifiers and SHAP, validated across regions. Female sex, perceived health and sleep disorders relate to all conditions.

title: Machine learning prediction of psychological resilience: An analysis of health and self-perception variables
summary_en: Predicts psychological resilience in 360 university students from diet, smoking, alcohol and body image with random forest and TabNet. Accuracy is moderate; perceived health and body image are the key predictors.

title: Social contact, social cohesion, and social safety outcomes of children's school travel
screening_reason: Children's school travel and social outcomes; not mental health analytics
summary_en: Uses a Bayesian belief network on 601 primary school children to relate school travel to social contact, cohesion and perceived safety.

title: Sophisticated bio-sensing architecture for anxiety identification using enhanced machine learning techniques
summary_en: Presents ANXIETY-CARE, an anxiety detection system based on sweat (electrodermal) sensors with XGBoost and CNN/LSTM models. The LSTM reaches 84.3% accuracy on the StudentLife dataset.

title: Using machine learning to predict child active transportation prevalence

title: Prevalence, persistence, and severity of 12-month and 30-day DSM-5 disorders in the World Mental Health Hong Kong Study

title: PUW! Cognitive strength in context: An innovative, multi-modal framework for real-time analysis of stress and socio-emotional functioning

title: Predictors of loneliness at school: An explainable artificial intelligence approach on a large-scale cross-cultural assessment
summary_en: Predicts loneliness at school in 60,498 students aged 10 and 15 (SSES survey) with elastic net, random forest, XGBoost and XAI. Bullying is the strongest predictor; extraversion and emotional stability are protective.

title: Railways to better minds: The influence of high-speed rail on cognitive health inequalities

title: AI-driven mixed-methods analysis of technology dependence: Personality-moderated pathways to Oral English anxiety in language learning

title: Identifying common disease trajectories of Alzheimer's disease with electronic health records

title: Predicting the student's perceptions of multi-domain environmental factors in a Norwegian school building: Machine learning approach

title: Disentangling doctoral well-being support in progress-focused workshops: Combining qualitative and quantitative data in single-case learning analytics
summary_en: Proposes single-case learning analytics combining quantitative and qualitative longitudinal data to assess well-being support in doctoral workshops (105 doctoral students), showing who benefits more or less.

title: Using machine learning algorithms to predict students' general self-efficacy in PISA 2018

title: Computerised adaptive method for assessing university undergraduates’ mental well-being within an African context: An open-source set-up with Concerto

title: MindLift: AI-powered mental health assessment for students
summary_en: Presents MindLift, a multimodal platform (behaviour, voice tone, facial expression, text sentiment) using CNN, RNN and transformer models with a CBT-based chatbot. Reports increased engagement but no specific metrics.

title: Enhancing the emotional aspects of language education through generative artificial intelligence (GenAI): A qualitative investigation
screening_reason: Qualitative interviews; no data analytics
summary_en: Qualitative interviews with 21 first-year university students and three instructors on how generative AI affects emotional engagement and well-being in language learning; GenAI is perceived to reduce anxiety and stress.

title: Optimising team dynamics: The role of AI in enhancing challenge-based learning participation experience and outcomes

summary_en: Uses random forest regression, neural networks and SEM on 524 undergraduates to relate mindfulness, psychological flexibility and rumination to mental health and well-being. Psychological flexibility and rumination mediate the effect of mindfulness.

summary_en: Detects depression in Bangladeshi university students with ML, deep learning and language models, handling imbalance with resampling. Random forest reaches 91.1% accuracy and RoBERTa 98.6% recall; SHAP and LIME explain predictions.

title: Artificial intelligence assisted identification of newborn auricular deformities via smartphone application

summary_en: Predicts perceived psychological and social stress in 444 university students during COVID-19 with supervised ML, PCA and hyperparameter optimisation. About 24% show extremely high psychological stress; the MLP reaches 80.5% accuracy.
